title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes construct, step by step, the profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, with a set of base points stable under the symmetry group S_3 (the group S_J, J = {0,1,infinity}) and under complex conjugation tau. They then describe the automorphisms u of this groupoid that fix the base points and commute with S_3. On the previous page such automorphisms of the level-II groupoid were encoded by data (rho, gamma, eta):
- rho is in Zhat^*, with gamma = (rho-1)/2;
- the remaining datum is alpha = l_0^gamma * beta, with beta = sigma_inf(eta) eta^{-1};
- the constraint is equation (24): alpha * rho^{-1}(alpha) * rho^{-2}(alpha) = 1, where rho also names the order-3 rotation acting on pihat_{0,3};
- for the arcs a~_i^omega one gets alpha~ = eta^{-1} l_0^gamma eps_0(eta).

This page.
(1) Equation (24) in alpha is equivalent to the same cyclic equation (26) in alpha~: alpha~ * rho^{-1}(alpha~) * rho^{-2}(alpha~) = 1. The two are related by the twisted conjugation (25 bis). The boxed formula (27), alpha~ = eta^{-1} l_0^gamma eps_0(eta), records the special form alpha~ takes when it comes from (eta, gamma).

(2) Groupoid III Pi_J. It is the groupoid induced by II Pi_J on the three base points Q_i, i in J. In the figure the Q_i lie on the three real intervals, presumably the transposition-fixed points; the points B_i^omega lie in the upper and lower half planes. It has:
- generators: the six oriented arcs a~_i^omega (omega = +,-);
- relations: the S_3-stable system (16) of six relations, of which only two are effective.
Complex conjugation tau fixes the Q_i and acts on the arcs (written tau a~_i^omega = (a~_i^omega)^{-1}).

(3) Main claim. An automorphism of III Pi_J that fixes the vertices and commutes with S_3 is the same thing as an element alpha~ in pihat_{0,3} satisfying (26). This is a presentation-level statement: the S_3-equivariance determines u from the image of one arc, written as a~ times psi(alpha~), and the two effective relations reduce to the single cyclic equation.

(4) Local monodromy. The loop lambda~_i^omega = a~_i^{omega'} a~_i^omega lies in pi(Q_{omega' i}) and is a small loop around a puncture, identified with l_0. Formula (29) gives u(lambda~) = psi(alpha~ eps_0(alpha~) l_0). With the special form (27) this becomes eta^{-1} l_0^p eta, where p = 2gamma+1 = rho. The next page concludes that u(l_0) is conjugate (by eta^{-1}) to l_0^rho. This is the statement that such automorphisms act on inertia generators through the 'cyclotomic' exponent rho, exactly as Galois elements do.

Purpose. Within the cote's programme ('Action de Galois sur Teichmüller') the page isolates the essential, local part of the Galois / Teichmüller-automorphism data in genus 0. These are the pairs (rho, alpha~) with rho in Zhat^* and gamma = (rho-1)/2, subject to an S_3-cyclic 'hexagon-type' equation. This is structurally the same as Drinfeld's later GT, defined by pairs (lambda, f) with m = (lambda-1)/2 and the hexagon relation.
errors: The identity alpha~ eps_0(alpha~) l_0 = eta^{-1} l_0^p eta does not follow from alpha~ = eta^{-1} l_0^gamma eps_0(eta) if eps_0 is a strict involution fixing l_0. One then gets eta^{-1} l_0^{2gamma} eta l_0, which needs eta to commute with l_0. It does hold if eps_0^2 = Inn(l_0^{±1}) (a 'semi-involution', natural for identifications via groupoid paths) or with a different ordering convention in (29). The conclusion u(l_0) ~ l_0^rho is correct; the displayed intermediate formula hides a convention.
The label (27) is used twice: for the boxed formula and for the tau-action. The labels (16), (26) and II/III superscripts are partly ambiguous on the manuscript.

The tau-action written as tau(a~_i^omega) = (a~_i^omega)^{-1} looks suspicious geometrically. Conjugation should swap the upper and lower routes (omega <-> omega') rather than invert an arc. It may be a slip or a shorthand.

ideas.what: Automorphisms of the S_3-symmetric profinite fundamental groupoid of P^1-{0,1,inf} fixing base points and commuting with S_3 are parametrized by (rho in Zhat^*, gamma=(rho-1)/2, alpha~ in pihat_{0,3}) subject to a cyclic (order-3) equation x rho^{-1}(x) rho^{-2}(x)=1
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GThat (hexagon relation with m=(lambda-1)/2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990s) for the profinite version
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) announces the 'Teichmüller tower' and the role of genus 0 with up to 4 points; it does not write the equations explicitly

ideas.what: Using three base points Q_i on the three real intervals (fixed by transpositions) plus points in the upper and lower half-planes, chosen stable under S_3 x {1, tau}, instead of tangential base points
ideas.modern_name: groupoid with S_3-symmetric (non-tangential) base points; cf. tangential base points (Deligne, Ihara)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tangential base points: Deligne 1989; symmetric groupoid viewpoint: Grothendieck (Esquisse), Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions 'groupoïdes fondamentaux' with base points stable under symmetries, in general terms

ideas.what: Derivation that such an automorphism sends the inertia loop l_0 to a conjugate of l_0^rho with p=2gamma+1=rho, conjugator eta^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: inertia (branch cycle) preservation by GT; cyclotomic character

ideas.what: Ansatz alpha~ = eta^{-1} l_0^gamma eps_0(eta): solutions of the cyclic equation coming from twisted 'coboundaries'
ideas.modern_name: f_sigma = p^{-1} sigma(p) form of Galois cocycles (Ihara's f_sigma via the path from 01 to 10)

missed.claim: The page raises, implicitly, whether every solution of the cyclic equation x rho^{-1}(x) rho^{-2}(x)=1 for the 3-vertex groupoid is of the twisted-coboundary form eta^{-1} l_0^gamma eps_0(eta). This amounts to a 'gauge-fixing' description of the set V of hexagon solutions, on which S_3 x {1,tau} acts by theta_g x = g·x^{sg(g)} (next page). This is not a standard way GT is presented in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible alternative parametrization of the hexagon component of GThat, based on S_3-symmetric real base points rather than tangential ones. It might clarify the relation between the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations. It is mostly of historical and expository value.

missed.claim: Explicit evidence, in dated-from-1978 manuscripts, of Grothendieck deriving GT-type equations: rho in Zhat^*, gamma=(rho-1)/2, an order-3 cyclic relation, and inertia acting as l_0 -> conj(l_0^rho). This comes from S_3-equivariant automorphisms of the genus-0 three-point groupoid, about a decade before Drinfeld's GT.
missed.quote: La donnée d'un automorphisme des groupoïdes III Π_J, fixant les sommets et commutant à S_J, équivaut à celle d'un α̃ ∈ Π̂_{0J} satisfaisant (26)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents in detail the oft-stated claim that Grothendieck anticipated GT. That anticipation is widely acknowledged, so the novelty is the explicit form, not the idea.

deep.surprise_reason: That Grothendieck anticipated GT is known. This page gives a concrete, pre-Drinfeld derivation of the hexagon-type equation with gamma=(rho-1)/2, an S_3 x conjugation-symmetric choice of real base points, and a coboundary ansatz. These are notable details but not a result absent in substance from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Boxed formula (27) reads α̃ = η^{-1} l_0^γ ε_0(η) (η, as on the previous page's (25)), not y; likewise 'provient de η, γ par (27)' and 'η^{-1} l_0^p η'.
(26) should read α̃ ρ^{-1}(α̃) ρ^{-2}(α̃) = 1 (by analogy with (24)); the hats in the transcription are spurious.
'sur l'un des trois sommets' is probably 'sur l'ens. des trois sommets Q_i'.
'se réduisant à en fait : deux relations effectives' should read 'et se réduisant en fait à deux relations effectives'.
'opère dans le graphe et relations' should read 'opère dans le graphe et ses relations'.
(28): λ̃_i^ω = ã_i^{ω'} ã_i^ω (the superscript 'ω'−ω' is a misreading).
